correctness.rationale: For all positive box half-lengths and Haar central planes, a section hits each coordinate-face pair iff the weighted normal coordinate is smaller than the sum of the other two, apart from a spherical null set. The six-face event is exactly a three-ray simplicial cone. An exact symbolic determinant and pairwise dot-product computation gives the displayed arctangent law via the standard, attributed spherical solid-angle theorem; 400 independent Girard-excess numerical comparisons and 720000 seeded Gaussian samples agree. Arithmetic–geometric mean yields \(Q/(abc)\ge5\sqrt2\), with equality only for equal half-lengths. Continuity of \(p_6(t,1,1)\) and its \(t\to\infty\) limit establish the full exact probability range. The proof establishes the entire positive real domain; simulations supplement and do not replace proof.

value.rationale: The invariant is the natural probability of hexagonal rather than parallelogram central sections under Haar orientation. An exact two-independent-aspect-ratio law is a complete, shape-sensitive benchmark, not a tabulation of one artificial input; the strict cubic optimizer, optimal numerical constant and attainable probability interval settle a motivated global comparison for all orthogonal boxes. Existing random cube section work gives only the cube point; recent orthotope width studies use the same geometry and spherical randomness but do not provide its combinatorial section statistics. No downstream general theorem is claimed or required.
